name: Brainiac
label: Touch and Go
lede: Four kids from Dayton with a Moog, noise and flashy 1970s stage clothes, who reportedly told Geffen where to go, got courted by Interscope, and lost their singer five days after he bought an old Mercedes.

eras.title: We'll Eat Anything
eras.text: Brainiac came out of Dayton, Ohio, the same small city as Guided by Voices and The Breeders, and sounded like neither: punk guitars, a battered Moog and a singer who changed voices mid-song. Within two years of the first show a major label was calling.

years.h: Brainiac forms in Dayton, Ohio
years.p: [[Tim Taylor|01a4d435-701d-47e4-b250-42bcd7bef7b8]] on vocals, keyboards and guitar, [[Juan Monasterio|b0aab1ff-b9f0-4fa7-addf-7308945bea43]] on bass, Michelle Bodine on guitar and [[Tyler Trent|1da43fc9-1e3c-4519-973c-34da0d3087eb]] on drums start Brainiac in Dayton in January 1992.

years.h: Brainiac's first show, as We'll Eat Anything, at Wright State
years.p: Brainiac's first gig is an opening slot for the Oxymorons at Wright State University's Rathskellar, played under the temporary name We'll Eat Anything.

years.src: Wikipedia: Smack Bunny Baby · Brainiac official site
years.h: Smack Bunny Baby, Brainiac's debut on Grass Records
years.p: Brainiac's first album, recorded at Excello Studios in Brooklyn with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] of [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]], is the only one with Michelle Bodine. Spin put it on its 1993 list of the ten best albums you didn't hear.
years.xp: Spin praised its fondness for Moog synth and its ear for buried melody. The LP came on turquoise-marbled vinyl and carried Velveteen, left off the CD. Craft Recordings reissued it for its 30th anniversary on December 1, 2023.

years.h: Brainiac reportedly turn down a £2 million Geffen offer
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Geffen's Gary Gersh offered Brainiac a £2 million deal soon after Smack Bunny Baby, and the band allegedly told him to fuck off.

years.h: Michelle Bodine leaves Brainiac; John Schmersal joins on guitar
years.p: Michelle Bodine quits Brainiac in November 1993 and later leads O-matic and Shesus. [[John Schmersal|9f0f837b-e427-4611-aef4-5db88298bfaf]] takes over guitar, keyboards and backing vocals.

eras.title: Bonsai Superstar
eras.text: With Eli Janney producing, Brainiac made records that broke on purpose: shorted mics, found voices, a chorus sung into a fan. Touch and Go signed them, Kim Deal produced them, and the opening slots got bigger.

years.h: Bonsai Superstar, produced by Girls Against Boys' Eli Janney
years.p: Brainiac record their second album at Plantain Studios in Brooklyn with Eli Janney. It's John Schmersal's first album with the band.
years.xp:
One song was cut in a basement with a cheap bullet mic that shorted out mid-vocal, and the feedback stayed in the mix. Voice samples on another came from a record found in a Knoxville, Tennessee store, and a chorus was sung into an electric fan to make it stutter.

According to Wikipedia, Pitchfork later ranked Bonsai Superstar No. 57 on its top 100 albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Brainiac on Lollapalooza's side stage and a John Peel session
years.p: Brainiac play the Lollapalooza side stage and record four songs in the UK for [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s BBC Radio 1 show.

years.h: Brainiac on the road with Beck, the Breeders and the Jesus Lizard
years.p: Brainiac's live shows build a buzz as they open tours for Beck, [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] and [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]].
years.xp: The bills ran the other way too: the Dayton Daily News notes that [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]] once opened for Brainiac in the 1990s, decades before Brainiac opened for Mogwai.

years.h: Internationale EP, produced by Kim Deal, on Touch and Go
years.p: Brainiac's first release for Touch and Go is a three-song EP produced by [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] of the Breeders and the Pixies: Go Freaks Go, Silver Iodine and Simon Says.

eras.title: Saturday Night Fever gone punk
eras.text: Brainiac's first Touch and Go album dressed the noise in flashy 1970s clothes and made them one of the most talked-about live bands in American indie rock. Elektra and Interscope started chasing them.

q: Make pop music that sounded futuristic so it wouldn't sound dated.
years.src: Wikipedia: Hissing Prigs in Static Couture
years.h: Hissing Prigs in Static Couture, Brainiac's last album
years.p: Mostly recorded at Water Music in Hoboken with Eli Janney; [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] cut Nothing Ever Changes in his basement. CMJ's Jenny Eliscu described Brainiac as Saturday Night Fever gone punk.
years.xp: On stage the band went for a 1970s fashion-band look in flashy outfits. Magnet later called the album a lost classic.

years.h: Tim Taylor's rule: if it sounds like a hit, wreck it
years.p: Juan Monasterio says Tim Taylor would bring a finished song to practice, and if anyone said it sounded like a radio hit, he'd return with a version nobody could recognize.
years.xp: Taylor was the son of jazz guitarist Terry Taylor and grew up loving the Beatles. He sang through Moog effects and switched vocal personas inside a single song.

years.h: Elektra and Interscope chase Brainiac
years.p: After Hissing Prigs, Brainiac get offers from Elektra and Interscope, and head toward a deal with Interscope.

eras.title: An EP, an Interscope deal, a 1972 Mercedes
eras.text: Brainiac cut a synth-heavy EP with Jim O'Rourke as a teaser for their major-label album and were deep in demos for it. Seven weeks after the EP came out, Tim Taylor was dead at 28 and the band was over.

years.h: Electro-Shock for President, produced by Jim O'Rourke
years.p: Brainiac's six-song EP, produced by [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]], is built mostly on electronics. It was meant as a teaser for a fourth album on Interscope.
years.xp: Juan Monasterio told Talkhouse the band had no plan to make an indie Brainiac album on Interscope. The demos for that album surfaced 26 years later as The Predator Nominate.

years.src: Wikipedia: Brainiac (band) · Talkhouse · Transmissions After Zero
years.h: Tim Taylor dies at 28 in his 1972 Mercedes, and Brainiac ends
years.p: Driving home, Tim Taylor crashed his 1972 Mercedes into a lamppost and the car caught fire. John Schmersal said toxicology showed carbon monoxide poisoning killed Taylor before the crash.
years.xp: The band later explained in Transmissions After Zero that the car had rusted badly enough to let exhaust into the passenger compartment. Taylor had bought it five days earlier, and was coming back from sessions for the Interscope album, Talkhouse reports.

years.src: I Heart the Noise · Talkhouse · setlist.fm · Wikipedia: Jeff Buckley
years.h: Jeff Buckley opens his last show talking about Tim Taylor
years.p: At Barristers in Memphis, [[Jeff Buckley|e6e879c0-3d56-4f12-b3c5-3ce459661a8e]] opens his final concert talking about Tim Taylor's death, according to I Heart the Noise and Talkhouse. Three days later Buckley drowned in the Wolf River.

years.h: A benefit for Tim Taylor with Guided by Voices and the Breeders
years.p: A few months after Tim Taylor's death, Dayton's [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]] and the Breeders play a benefit show in his memory.

eras.title: Rewiring other people's bands
eras.text: The survivors scattered into other projects while Brainiac's reputation grew without them. Trent Reznor, the Mars Volta, Muse and the National all pointed back to them, and a Kickstarter-funded documentary finally told the story.

years.h: John Schmersal forms Enon; Tyler Trent drums for the Breeders
years.p: John Schmersal makes a solo record as John Stuart Mill, then starts [[Enon|ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06]]. Tyler Trent briefly drums in the Breeders, and Juan Monasterio turns to directing music videos.

years.src: Wikipedia: Brainiac (band) · Wikipedia: Electro-Shock for President
years.h: Trent Reznor uses Electro-Shock for President as a guide
years.p: [[Trent Reznor|bc880664-6751-4998-984d-ebdbff15d229]] called Brainiac really inspiring sonically and used the Electro-Shock for President EP as a reference for [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]]' 2005 album With Teeth.
years.xp: Cedric Bixler-Zavala and Omar Rodríguez-López of [[At the Drive-In|7e13cd1c-0300-4d03-bd8e-5f86dd99d74f]] and [[The Mars Volta|20883363-1ea4-4d72-ad72-c0e767038f3e]] cited the same EP. Matt Bellamy said part of [[Muse|9c9f1380-2516-4fc9-a3e6-f9f61941d090]]'s Exo-Politics owed Brainiac a debt, Chris Walla named them for [[Death Cab for Cutie|0039c7ae-e1a7-4a7d-9b49-0cbc716821a6]]'s Narrow Stairs, and [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]]'s Matt Berninger said they'd rewire your idea of a rock band.

years.h: Brainiac's survivors play a secret show at Blind Bob's
years.p: Juan Monasterio, Tyler Trent and John Schmersal quietly reunite for an unannounced show at Blind Bob's in Dayton, the Dayton Daily News reported.

years.src: Dayton Daily News · The Current · Wikipedia: Brainiac (band)
yt: Brainiac: Transmissions After Zero, SXSW trailer (2019)
years.h: Transmissions After Zero, the Brainiac documentary, premieres
years.p: Eric Mahoney's Kickstarter-funded film premieres at the Neon in Dayton and screens at SXSW, with Steve Albini, Matt Berninger, Melissa Auf der Maur, David Yow and Taylor's mother and sister.
years.xp: It came out on DVD and streaming on February 21, 2020. Wikipedia notes favorable reviews.

years.src: Dayton Daily News · Talkhouse · Wikipedia: Brainiac (band)
years.h: Brainiac play again, with Tim Krug, for the film
years.p: Juan Monasterio, Tyler Trent and John Schmersal play shows in New York, Los Angeles and at the Brightside in Dayton with Tim Krug. The sets include two songs nobody had heard before.

eras.title: Back on stage with Mogwai
eras.text: Twenty-five years after Tim Taylor's death, the survivors dug out the demos for the album that never happened and went on tour with a band that used to open for them.

q: Brainiac's last concerted effort, our last complete thought, before the end.
years.h: The Predator Nominate: Brainiac's lost 1997 demos
years.p: Touch and Go releases nine Brainiac demos from 1997, made for the Interscope debut, with Tim Taylor singing. It's their first new music in almost 26 years.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Predator Nominate · Wikipedia: Brainiac (band)
years.h: Brainiac open for Mogwai in the UK
years.p: Brainiac support [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]] on UK dates, with John Schmersal singing lead and Tim Krug on guitar, and add headline shows of their own.

years.src: Wikipedia: Smack Bunny Baby · Brainiac official site
years.h: Smack Bunny Baby reissued for its 30th birthday
years.p: Craft Recordings puts Brainiac's 1993 debut Smack Bunny Baby back in print on green vinyl and streaming after decades away.

years.h: Brainiac kick off a tour at Dayton's Brightside
years.p: Brainiac start a spring tour at the Brightside in Dayton, then join Mogwai for an East Coast run. Tyler Trent says the band has been in a new phase since 2023.

years.h: Brainiac share a bill with Guided by Voices in Athens
years.p: Brainiac play the Athens Community Arts and Music Festival in Ohio alongside fellow Daytonians Guided by Voices.

years.h: Brainiac play a KEXP session in Seattle
years.p: On a West Coast run, Brainiac record a six-song live session for Seattle radio station KEXP.
